column3: Close to the Greek; “take courage” is rendered “be of good cheer.”
NKJV has “knowing their thoughts” where the Greek here reads “seeing their thoughts.”
Close to the Greek; “authority” is rendered “power,” and “mat” as “bed.”
NKJV has “marveled,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “were afraid.” “Authority” is rendered “power.”
NKJV moves “Jesus” to the subject of “sat at the table” and has “with Him”; the Greek says “He reclined … with Jesus.”
NKJV includes “to repentance,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “but sinners.”
NKJV renders “the sons of the bridechamber” as “the friends of the bridegroom.”
Close to the Greek; “kneeling down to” is rendered “worshiped.”
Close to the Greek; “fringe” is rendered “hem.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV adds “wailing” to describe the crowd.
Close to the Greek; “go away” is rendered “make room.”
